A ~Z session on site Z cannot see, address, or be addressed by the fabric on Andrew's laptop over MCP: get_live_agents() on site Z returned 1 (itself) while 1.0.0_SA_CTO, 3.0.0_SA_CVO, 0.2.0_DT and 0.4.0_DE were provably alive on the laptop, evidenced by 11 pushes in the preceding 60 minutes. THE FABRIC HAS NO CROSS-DEVICE LIVENESS ORACLE AND NO CROSS-DEVICE DELIVERY CHANNEL; today the ONLY working cross-device transport is the git trunk (committed message files under org/mcp/inbox/**, proven both directions 2026-07-29), which is a HISTORY tier, not a delivery tier -- it requires a human-or-loop-driven pull and has no ack, no ordering, no backlog signal.

hazards: RESOLVED 2026-07-29 by CTO arch-gate LD-0347 -- AND THE HAZARD AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN WAS ITSELF WRONG AT ITS PREMISE, which is the more useful half of this record. It read: 'NFRA_AGENTBUS_PRD.md:105-108 designs Port 2 on DynamoDB; this project builds SQS; that is a transport substitution against a design ratified ~5h earlier; the PRD needs a real amendment through CTO -- it has not had one.' THE FALSE PREMISE: eff96f5079, the very commit cited as Port 2's ratification, IS the act that CHANGED the transport to SQS. Its body and LD-0306's ratification_note both state it verbatim -- 'THE RATIFIED DESIGN IS NOT THE DRAFTED ONE ... Ratified shape = SQS FIFO queue-pair' -- with the DDB design recorded as the superseded 07-17 DRAFT. So there was never a substitution to bless: these queues ARE Port 2's transport, and the PRD's DynamoDB cell was the STALE RECORD, not the binding one. HOW THE ERROR PROPAGATED, recorded because it is structural and will recur: LD-0306's decision_summary describes the DRAFTED design while its ratification_note (a different field, further down the same file) describes the RATIFIED one, and nothing marks the summary stale -- so a reader who stops at the summary, which is what a summary field invites, gets a superseded design carrying full ledger authority. MSTR stopped there; CTO~Z drafted a parallel-channel REFUSAL from the same premise and reversed it only after reading the ratification field and commit body at source (Rule 22). A CTO arch-gate formally refusing a transport the sovereign ratified 6h earlier came within one document-read of landing in the PRD as law. RESOLUTION: NFRA_AGENTBUS_PRD.md AMENDMENT B -- transport cell :108 and status cell :112 corrected, A.3 design-source + WS-1 reshaped off DDB semantics, A.5 marked superseded as to transport, O-3 qualified, O-5 opened for the one capability a queue-pair cannot carry (CLAIM/cross-site HALTGT, now FENCED: no agent may report an enforced cross-site halt on this channel).

MSTR BUILT THIS ITSELF, against Constitution Art. VI (govern through the org) and the Stakes Matrix S3 rule that post-ratification execution runs the normal Tier-1 chain, never MSTR. The justification is specific and does not generalize: the Tier-1 chain is UNREACHABLE from site Z over MCP, which is the very defect this project exists to fix. Do not cite this as precedent for MSTR executing S3 work whenever a chain is inconvenient -- the discriminator is structural unreachability, measured, not latency.

SITE-Z INSTANCES TAKE A ~Z SUFFIX FOR ATTRIBUTION, NOT FOR COLLISION-SAFETY -- and the distinction is recorded because MSTR~Z first claimed the wrong one. The initial claim was that spawning a bare Tier-1 serial on site Z would reproduce the dual-COO GA-3 collision. Andrew challenged it and it does not survive: GA-3's mechanism REQUIRES a shared broker plus a shared filesystem (two streams racing one inbox's mv). Measured across these devices, neither exists -- org/mcp/liveness.json is gitignored (.gitignore:237) so liveness is device-local, the broker is localhost:7800 per-device, and org/mcp/inbox/* is gitignored with ZERO tracked files in 1.0.0_SA_CTO's inbox. Two same-named CTOs on two devices would not collide; they would be INVISIBLE TO EACH OTHER, which is this project's problem statement, not a hazard. What genuinely survives is weaker: git author-line ambiguity (both commit as 1.0.0_SA_CTO, so history cannot attribute a commit to a device) and duplicated work by two agents unaware of each other. Andrew's ruling: use ~Z. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is why this stays in the record: a named failure mode is not portable to a new topology until its MECHANISM is checked against that topology -- reasoning from the NAME of a hazard rather than its mechanism is how a false constraint gets minted, and a false constraint is not a safe error, it distorts the design around it.

SILENT SAME-DEVICE INTERCEPTION -- AND ACK-BY-MessageId CANNOT DETECT IT (found live 2026-07-29 ~1900Z, both MSTR instances + 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps concurring). LD-0347/PRD B.4a ruled that the bus addresses DEVICES, not AGENTS. The consequence nobody had written down is sharper than the ruling: ON A DEVICE THAT HAS A LIVE CONSUMER, A BUS MESSAGE ADDRESSED TO ANY OTHER AGENT ON THAT DEVICE IS SILENTLY INTERCEPTED BY WHOEVER IS DRAINING -- and the sender's ack discipline returns a VALID ACK FROM THE WRONG AGENT. EXERCISED, not theorised: MSTR~Z sent MessageId 2e3babbe addressed to 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps; 0.0.0_AB_MSTR's consumer drained it; AE would NEVER have seen it and only received it because MSTR hand-relayed over MCP. Had MSTR not disclosed who acked, ~Z would have recorded delivery-to-AE holding a correct receipt. **THIS IS THE INVERSE OF RULE 22b's KNOWN LIMIT, AND THE PAIR IS THE POINT: 22b says an ack proves the agent read the CONTENT but not that this TRANSPORT delivered it; this says an ack proves SOME agent read it but NOT THAT IT WAS THE ADDRESSED ONE. Both halves of an addressed-delivery claim fail, in opposite directions, and the oracle looks clean in both.** Mitigation is NOT more ack machinery -- it is that per Andrew's ~1815Z standing rule site Z does not route work to the main fabric at all, so the addressed-cross-device-dispatch case should not arise. Where a cross-device message MUST name a specific agent, delivery is establishable only by an ack whose SENDER SERIAL EQUALS THE ADDRESSED SERIAL (B.4a's own condition 3), never by an ack merely naming the MessageId.

An SQS queue is a resource that COSTS and PERSISTS. It is created here outside the normal Terraform path at Andrew's explicit frontrun instruction; it must be brought under Terraform by the owning lane (AE-cloud/CTO) rather than left as console/CLI-drift, or it becomes exactly the untracked-infra class the estate keeps paying for.

Where a helpful peer can hand-carry content out of band, the ack oracle silently certifies the WRONG PROPOSITION, and does so more confidently the more cooperative everyone is being.
